description: COMBINE the global-best kernel (brief 0 HEAD 90eeb8f8, 6407us) with brief 2's specialized fused tiny-n Householder megakernel (186ad6fec) for the launch-bound small shapes. Brief 2 got n=32 B=20 -> 32.8us (9.8x), n=176 B=40 -> 558us (39x), n=352 B=40 -> 6377us (8.0x) with a one-CTA-per-matrix unblocked-in-SMEM kernel (odd-padded LDA=n|1 to kill bank conflicts; these shapes are CTA-barrier-bound + SM-starved, compute <10%, so NOT tensor-core-bound). The current best routes n=176/352 through its large-n-oriented panel kernel; adopt brief 2's tiny-n megakernel for whichever of n in {32,176,352} it measures FASTER per-shape than the current best, keeping the best's n>=512 path unchanged. AVOID the substring 'stream' anywhere in submission.py incl. comments (leaderboard ban-scan matches it).

COMBINE: integrate parent B fused tiny-n megakernel (qr_unblocked, whole matrix in odd-padded SMEM LDA=n|1, single fused launch) into parent A blocked-panel kernel via one load_inline. Routed n in {32,176} to megakernel, kept n in {352,512,1024} on parent A path UNCHANGED, off-grid->geqrf. Per-shape: n=32 90.3->33.0us (2.74x), n=176 635->561us (1.13x), n=352 1614us kept on parent A (parent B was 6377us there). n>=512 unchanged within noise. Geomean 6402->5828us (-9.0%). nsys confirms n=176 is now 1 qr_unblocked launch/matrix (was 11 panel + GEMMs). All 22 tests + diff/invariance/offgrid guards + kernelguard CLEAN.

Tune megakernel block threads for n=176: swept T in {256,512,384}. T=384 measured best (n=176 556.8us vs T=512 560.9us vs T=256 563.1us), reproduced across 2 runs (geomean 5817/5819). n=32 keeps T=128. Geomean 5828->5818us. All tests + diff/invariance/offgrid guards + kernelguard CLEAN.

Confirm n=32 megakernel is barrier-bound: swept n=32 block threads T in {64,96,128}, all ~33us (T=128/64 tied best 32.8us, T=96 34.8us); n=32 limited by serial 32-col 2-barrier chain not thread count. Kept T=128 (n=32) + T=384 (n=176). Comment-only vs trial 2; geomean 5818us reproduced (shapes: n=32 32.8us, n=176 556.8us, n=352 1612.9us). nsys: n=176 is 1 qr_unblocked launch/matrix, 100% GPU. All tests + diff/invariance/offgrid guards + kernelguard CLEAN.

COMBINE done: parent B's fused tiny-n megakernel integrated onto parent A in one load_inline. Best commit 131d8ada2, geomean 6406.8->5818.2us (-9.2% / 1.101x), all 22 tests + diff/invariance/offgrid guards + kernelguard CLEAN; n>=512 path byte-unchanged from parent A. Per-shape vs parent A measured this run: n=32 90.3->32.8us (2.75x, megakernel), n=176 635.4->556.8us (1.14x, megakernel, T=384), n=352 kept on parent A 1614us (parent B's panel-blocked path was 6377us there - the n=352 matrix overruns the 224KB SMEM cap so its megakernel falls back to a slower L2-resident block kernel). nsys confirms n=176 collapsed from 11 panel_factor launches + 3 cuBLAS GEMMs per matrix to ONE qr_unblocked launch (100% GPU). Knob sweeps: n=176 threads {256,384,512}->384 best (small ~0.7% win); n=32 threads {64,96,128} all ~33us (barrier-bound on the serial 32-col 2-barrier chain, not thread-bound). OPEN directions for the manager (not pursued, off this combine's scope): (1) n=352 is the largest remaining tiny-shape lever at 1614us and is NEITHER parent's strength - a megakernel variant that tiles the n=352 matrix across MULTIPLE CTAs or uses a 2-pass SMEM panel (rows split) could beat parent A's 1614us where the single-CTA full-SMEM megakernel cannot fit; (2) the n=176 megakernel still pays 2 barriers/column over 176 serial columns - a wider micro-panel (rank-k) inside the megakernel could cut the barrier count like parent A's 2-level panel does; (3) n=32's serial barrier chain (32 cols x 2 barriers) is the floor at 32.8us - a true batched-Jacobi or a warp-per-matrix layout (multiple tiny matrices per CTA) might amortize launch+barrier cost further since n=32 is deeply SM-starved (only 20 matrices on 148 SMs).
